input.prompt: An authentic Srikalahasti kalamkari hand-painted textile panel, photographed flat and straight-on so the cloth fills the entire frame edge to edge. Subject: a flowering Tree of Life rising from a small mound of earth, its curling branches spreading into a dome-shaped canopy of lotus blossoms, mango-shaped paisley leaves and buds. Two peacocks stand facing each other at the foot of the tree, one on each side, tails sweeping down in long patterned trains. Between the peacocks, at the base of the trunk, two round plates of thambulam: betel leaves, bananas, a coconut and flowers, with two small gold rings resting on one plate. Small parrots perch in the branches; a few tiny fish swim in a band of stylised water along the bottom. A dense ornamental border runs around all four edges: a lotus-and-vine scroll between two thin bands of dotted pattern. Style: freehand kalam (bamboo pen) outlines in iron-black with confident, slightly irregular line weight; flat natural vegetable-dye fills only: deep madder red (alizarin, brick red), indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, green made from indigo over yellow, and areas of undyed ecru cotton; dense hand-drawn fill patterns of dots, cross-hatching, scales and tiny petals; visible hand-woven cotton weave and slight dye bleed at the edges of colour areas; the ground of the panel is dyed deep madder red. Completely flat, no perspective, no shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism. No text, no letters, no writing, no numbers, no lamps, no diyas, no candles, no fire, no flames.
